articles.title: Do Freelancers Exporting Services Need GST Registration?
articles.dek: You will be told that invoicing a foreign client compels registration from the first rupee. Notification 10/2017 says otherwise for services under ₹20 lakh.

articles.title: Direct vs Regular Mutual Fund Plans: What the Gap Actually Costs
articles.dek: Same fund, same manager, same portfolio — one costs about 1.2 points a year more. Over 25 years at ₹10,000 a month that gap came to ₹32.80 lakh, more than the total invested.

articles.title: Marginal Relief Above ₹12 Lakh: The Band Where a Raise Earns You Nothing
articles.dek: Cross ₹12,00,000 of taxable income by ₹10,000 and you owe ₹10,400, not ₹63,960. Marginal relief removes the cliff — but leaves a ₹71,000 band taxed at 104%.

articles.title: Does Your Spouse's Income Count for Income-Driven Repayment?
articles.dek: Filing separately keeps a spouse income out of every current plan — but RAP narrowed the dependent rule, and separate filing costs six tax breaks.

articles.title: Debt Snowball vs. Avalanche: Which Payoff Method Actually Saves You More
articles.dek: Both methods put every spare dollar toward debt. The difference is which debt gets that dollar first — and it changes both how much interest you pay and how fast it feels like you're winning.

articles.title: Student Loan Repayment Changed July 2026: What RAP Means for Your Payment
articles.dek: SAVE, PAYE, and ICR are gone for new borrowers, replaced by two plans: RAP and the Tiered Standard Plan. Here's how each one calculates your payment, with a real worked example.

articles.title: The New 401(k) Roth Catch-Up Rule: What Changes for High Earners in 2026
articles.dek: If you're 50 or older and earned more than $150,000 last year, your 401(k) catch-up contributions just lost their upfront tax deduction. Here's exactly how the new rule works.

articles.title: Why Credit Card Rates Are Still Near 21% After Three Fed Rate Cuts
articles.dek: The Fed has cut its benchmark rate three times since 2025, but the average credit card still charges close to 21% — near an all-time high. Here's why, and what actually lowers your cost.

articles.title: Mortgage Rates Stuck Near 6.5% in 2026 — What the New Housing Law Does
articles.dek: Rates aren't expected to move much for the rest of the year. A sweeping new housing bill became law anyway, aimed at a different problem entirely: how many homes actually get built.

articles.title: India's New Income Tax Act 2025: Slabs, Rebate & What Changes
articles.dek: India's Income Tax Act 2025 takes effect April 1, 2026. Here's the new-regime slab structure, how the ₹12.75 lakh tax-free threshold actually works, and what it means for your filing.

articles.title: ECB Raises Rates for the First Time Since 2023: What It Means
articles.dek: The ECB hiked rates in June 2026, its first increase since 2023, with another decision due July 24. Here's why, what's next, and what it means for eurozone mortgages and savings.

articles.title: Africa's Interest Rates Are Moving in Opposite Directions in 2026
articles.dek: Nigeria is holding at 26.5%, Kenya is cutting toward 8.75%, and South Africa just hiked to 7%. Here's why Africa's biggest economies are diverging on rates, and what it means for borrowers and savers.

articles.title: The UK's 2026 Tax Changes: Dividend Tax Hikes, Frozen Allowances & ISAs
articles.dek: No single dramatic tax hike this year — instead, a dividend rate increase, allowances frozen through 2030, and a bigger ISA change already locked in for 2027. Here's what actually moves your numbers.

articles.title: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25% Again: What It Means for Mortgages
articles.dek: The Bank of Canada held its policy rate at 2.25% for a sixth straight decision in July 2026, while cutting its growth forecast. Here's what that means for variable-rate mortgages.

articles.title: Will the RBA Hike Rates Again in August 2026?
articles.dek: The RBA has already hiked three times in 2026, taking the cash rate to 4.35%. Economists are split on whether August brings a fourth hike toward a possible 4.85% peak.

articles.title: Japan Hikes, China Holds: Asia's Diverging Rate Paths in 2026
articles.dek: The Bank of Japan raised rates to 1.0% in June 2026 while China's central bank held its key rates at record lows for a 13th straight month. Why the two largest Asian economies are moving in opposite directions.

articles.title: Brazil Cuts Selic to 14.25% Even as Inflation Forecasts Rise
articles.dek: Brazil's central bank has cut the Selic rate three times in 2026 to 14.25%, even as its own inflation forecast rose to 5.2% — well above target. Here's the tension driving the disconnect.

articles.title: ACA Premiums Jump 114% in 2026 as Enhanced Subsidies Expire
articles.dek: Enhanced ACA premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025. Subsidized enrollees now pay 114% more on average — here's what changed, why, and how to check where you land.

articles.title: The NHS Modernisation Bill 2026: What's Actually Changing
articles.dek: The NHS Modernisation Bill, introduced to Parliament in May 2026, abolishes NHS England and creates a single patient record — the biggest NHS restructuring in over a decade. Here's what it does.

articles.title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY in 2026: ₹10 Lakh Cover for Seniors
articles.dek: Ayushman Bharat's Vay Vandana Card now gives every senior citizen 70+ a free ₹5 lakh top-up — ₹10 lakh total family cover. Here's how PM-JAY's 2026 expansion actually works.

articles.title: WHO's First GLP-1 Obesity Guideline, Explained
articles.dek: The World Health Organization published its first guideline on GLP-1 therapies for adult obesity in December 2025. Here's what it actually says — and doesn't say.

articles.title: Australia's Medicare Bulk Billing Changes From July 2026
articles.dek: From July 1, 2026, GPs no longer have to co-sign every bulk-billed Medicare form — patients can consent digitally instead. Here's what's changing and what it means at your next visit.

articles.title: What GLP-1 Drugs Actually Cost in 2026: US, UK, India & EU
articles.dek: The same GLP-1 weight-loss injection costs $50/month on US Medicare, £122 on the NHS, ₹5,660 in India, or up to €300 out of pocket in Germany. Here's why the price varies this much by country.

articles.title: US Stock Market 2026: Records, Rotation & Nvidia's $5T Run
articles.dek: The Dow topped 53,000, the Russell 2000 just had its best first half since 1991, and Nvidia briefly hit a $5.3 trillion valuation. Here's what's actually driving the 2026 US market — and the one stock everyone's watching.

articles.title: China Stock Market 2026: The AI Rally & Biren's 120% IPO Debut
articles.dek: Hong Kong's Hang Seng is up almost 30% in 2026, household savings are pouring out of bank deposits into stocks, and an AI chip IPO just surged 120% on debut. Here's what's actually driving China's market this year.

articles.title: Japan Stock Market 2026: Record Nikkei & the AI Chip Test Stock
articles.dek: The Nikkei is up 33% in 2026 and just posted its biggest quarterly gain since records began in 1965 — even as the Bank of Japan keeps raising rates. Here's what's driving it, and the chip-testing stock riding the AI wave.

articles.title: India Stock Market 2026: Record Sensex & the Jio IPO Wait
articles.dek: Sensex and Nifty are near record highs and analysts see more room to run in 2026 — but the stock everyone's actually talking about is Reliance, on the back of the Jio Platforms IPO filing. Here's the real picture.

articles.title: UK Stock Market 2026: FTSE Records & the Rolls-Royce Turnaround
articles.dek: The FTSE 100 is up 19.3% in 2026, powered by banks, miners, and defence stocks staying out of the AI-hype whipsaw — and Rolls-Royce has become the defining UK equity story of the last three years. Here's what's driving it.

articles.title: How Credit Card Interest Is Actually Calculated
articles.dek: Your APR isn't the rate you're charged — it's divided by 365 and applied daily, compounding as it goes. The real arithmetic, why the grace period vanishes the moment you carry a balance, and what the minimum payment costs.

articles.title: The Fed Has Held Rates All Year: What It Means for You
articles.dek: The federal funds rate has sat at 3.50–3.75% since December under new chair Kevin Warsh — yet the 30-year mortgage just hit its highest level since August 2025. Why those aren't a contradiction.

articles.title: 2026 IRS Limits: 401(k), IRA and Standard Deduction
articles.dek: You can put $24,500 in a 401(k) this year, and $35,750 if you're 60 to 63. Every number that changed, the four-year window most people miss, and what the extra room is worth once it compounds.

articles.title: HRA Exemption 2026: 8 Metro Cities Now at 50%
articles.dek: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad became metros for House Rent Allowance on 1 April 2026. Because the exemption is the lowest of three figures, whether you save anything depends entirely on which one was limiting you.

articles.title: EPF vs PPF vs NPS in 2026: Which Actually Builds More
articles.dek: EPF pays 8.25% with employer money attached, PPF pays 7.1% tax-free, NPS pays whatever the market gives. They differ on lock-in, guarantees, and which deductions survive under the new regime.

articles.title: CTC vs In-Hand Salary in India 2026: The Full Breakdown
articles.dek: A ₹18 lakh package pays ₹1,18,126 a month. Between the offer letter and your bank account sit two contributions you never see, one lump sum you might never collect, and a tax bill.

articles.title: RAP vs IBR: Where Each Plan Is Cheaper (2026 Study)
articles.dek: We computed both income-driven repayment plans across every income from $0 to $300,000 and 20 household types. RAP is cheaper in three of them, and never by more than $50.50 a month — while IBR can win by $554.50.

articles.title: The Advance Tax Cliff: Why ₹100 Short on 15 September Costs ₹1,083
articles.dek: At 1% a month, deferring advance tax costs a reasonable 12% a year. But s.234C attaches a 36% trigger to the September instalment, and missing it by ₹100 costs ₹1,083 on a ₹4 lakh liability.

articles.title: ITR Deadlines Split in 2026: Who Files by 31 July, Who Gets to 31 August
articles.dek: The Finance Act 2026 amended Section 139(1) so non-audit ITR-3 and ITR-4 filers now have until 31 August. Salaried filers still face 31 July — and the deciding factor is not your form, it is your audit position.

articles.title: RBI Holds Repo Rate at 5.25% for a Fourth Meeting
articles.dek: On 5 August the MPC held again and kept the stance neutral — while cutting FY27 inflation to 5.0% and lifting growth to 6.7%. Better numbers, same decision, and there is a reason for that.

articles.title: The Student Loan Deadlines That Move You Into RAP Automatically
articles.dek: PAYE and ICR sunset on 1 July 2028 and new PAYE enrolments end a year earlier. Borrowers who do not choose are placed in RAP by default — which our study found is the cheaper plan in only three of twenty household types.

articles.title: The Fed Held Again — But Three Officials Voted to Raise Rates
articles.dek: The FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 3.50–3.75% on a 9–3 vote. All three dissenters wanted a hike, not a cut — and the statement blames supply shocks in energy, the same diagnosis the RBI gave six weeks ago.

articles.title: Prepay the Loan or Invest the Difference? We Found the Exact Crossover
articles.dek: We modelled both choices over a full loan term at every return from 1% to 25%, at six different loan rates. The break-even landed within 0.1 percentage points of the loan rate itself, every time.

articles.title: How Much Do You Actually Need to Retire? The 4% Rule Is Now 3.9%
articles.dek: Morningstar puts the 2026 safe withdrawal rate at 3.9% for fixed spending. Applied honestly with inflation, funding a ₹50,000-a-month lifestyle 25 years out needs ₹6.6 crore, not ₹1.5 crore.

articles.title: SIP vs Lump Sum: The Question Most People Are Actually Asking Is Different
articles.dek: Vanguard found lump-sum investing beat phasing in about two thirds of the time. That finding says nothing about a SIP funded from salary — and conflating the two is why this debate never resolves.

articles.title: What Actually Moves Your Credit Score — and What Does Nothing
articles.dek: Payment history is 35% of a FICO score and amounts owed 30%. Most of the advice people follow targets the 10% categories, and closing an old card actively hurts two of them.

articles.title: ACA Premiums: Insurers Want Another 14% for 2027
articles.dek: Preliminary filings point to a second consecutive double-digit rise, on top of the 20% finalised for 2026. What that does to your bill, and the one lever most households still have.

articles.title: Old vs New Tax Regime: The Crossover Points, FY 2026-27
articles.dek: We computed the actual boundaries rather than working an example. The old regime wins in two separate salary bands, not one — and between them the new regime wins even with deductions maxed.
